knowledge_point.title: Integrating the Sum of a Reciprocal Function and a Power Function

question.:question/problem: Calculate $\int \frac{2{x}^{2}-4}{2x}\,dx.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2{x}^{2}-4}{2x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{2{x}^{2}}{2x}-\frac{2}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =\int (1x-\frac{2}{x})\text{d}x \\  & =1\int x\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-2\ln|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x>0 for radicals/fractional powers; x!=0 for integer rational forms, on connected intervals avoiding poles

question.:question/problem: Calculate $\int ({x}^{5/2}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{-1})\,\text{d}x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we apply the sum rule and get

$$
\int ({x}^{5/2}+\frac{1}{4}{x}^{-1})\,\text{d}x=\int {x}^{5/2}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x
$$

Now, using the power rule in the first term, and taking out the coefficient in the second term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{5/2}\,\text{d}x+\frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{5/2+1}}{\frac{5}{2}+1}+\frac{1}{4}\ln|x|+C \\  & =\frac{2}{7}{x}^{7/2}+\frac{1}{4}\ln|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the integral of ${(8-\frac{5}{x})}^{2}$ with respect to $x.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expanding the binomial and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {(8-\frac{5}{x})}^{2}\text{d}x & =\int (64-\frac{80}{x}+\frac{25}{{x}^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =\int 64\,\text{d}x-\int \frac{80}{x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{25}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =64\int \text{d}x-80\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+25\int \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =64x-80\ln|x|+25\frac{{x}^{-2+1}}{-2+1}+C \\  & =64x-80\ln|x|-\frac{25}{x}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Simplifying the exponents and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}{\sqrt{{x}^{7}}}-6{x}^{-1})\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{{x}^{7/2-5/2}}\,\text{d}x-6\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-6\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3\ln|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Simplifying the exponents and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}{\sqrt{{x}^{7}}}-14{x}^{-1})\text{d}x & =4\int \frac{1}{{x}^{7/2-5/2}}\,\text{d}x-14\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-14\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-10\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-10\ln|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Simplifying the exponents and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (5\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}{\sqrt{{x}^{7}}}-23{x}^{-1})\text{d}x & =5\int \frac{1}{{x}^{7/2-5/2}}\,\text{d}x-23\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-23\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-18\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-18\ln|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Simplifying the exponents and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (7\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}{\sqrt{{x}^{7}}}-15{x}^{-1})\text{d}x & =7\int \frac{1}{{x}^{7/2-5/2}}\,\text{d}x-15\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =7\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-15\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-8\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-8\ln|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Simplifying the exponents and applying the sum and constant factor rules, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{7}}}{\sqrt{{x}^{9}}}-3{x}^{-1})\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{x}^{9/2-7/2}}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x-3\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2\ln|x|+C.\end{aligned}
$$
